headline: Hospitality across the Americas, screened for a construction printer.
headline_html:
Hospitality across the Americas,
screened for a construction printer.
sub: Three counts per firm: repetition, open land, and a track record of paying for a new building method. Canada to Argentina.
meta_description: Hotel groups, operators, developers, architects and owners building hospitality from Canada to Argentina, screened against three counts for a construction printer.

group_notes.icon: Built or designed with ICON. Each tie names the project and the ICON page.
group_notes.adopter: A printed hotel under way, or printed buildings drawn.
group_notes.a: Hotel groups, operators and developers. Architects, contractors and owners sit apart.
group_notes.arch: They draw the walls. The counts judge the work they have built.
group_notes.trade: The counts judge the wall or the module they make.
group_notes.capital: Owns or funds. Its developers and operators build.
group_notes.rest: Two or three counts read No.

matrix.x_label: Repetition: builds the same unit more than once
matrix.y_label: Open land: builds outside a city

matrix_note: 65 firms read Yes on both axes of this grid. The grid leaves out track record. 42 of the 65 hold all three counts.
stat_strip: hotel groups, operators and developers hold all three counts
limits: Firms that build, own, run, design or fund hotels, resorts, lodges, villas, cabins and branded residences, from Canada to Argentina. Brokers and associations are left out. 27 countries.
Firm sites, company filings, trade press and tourism ministry reports, read June and September 2026. A firm stays when its own site or a cited page names it.
A founder, chief executive, president, chair, managing partner or owner, or a head of development, design, construction or real estate.
Each contact names its page: 411 named on a firm site or dated report, 216 with a LinkedIn profile. No aggregator. No URL constructed.

method.title: Counts on the page
method.text: Every count is a count of the records behind the page, at build time.

method.title: Yes, Partly, No
method.text: Each verdict carries its reason. Partly: partial evidence. No: no record, not a finding against the firm. Yes and Partly hold a count. No does not.

method.title: Figures
method.text: A figure in a firm's text is kept only when it is on a page the firm's card cites.

icon_record.line: Texas housing, Army barracks, a NASA habitat, and 2019 homes in Nacajuca, Tabasco. In hospitality, El Cosmico in Marfa. Titan is its system for outside builders.
facts: $899K for printer and pump. Material $620 a cubic yard. CODEX designs $2K to $5K. Deliveries beginning in 2027, per ICON's Titan page.
ICON sells Titan. The builder owns it and prints its own walls.
263 structures built since 2017, per ICON's site, September 2026.

Nacajuca, Tabasco, with New Story and Échale: the first two homes unveiled in 2019, printed with the Vulcan II. ICON's release: 50 homes planned. World Housing's page: 10 printed homes and 90 block homes.

Liz Lambert's hotel, designed by BIG. Ground broke September 2024, with 43 hotel units and 18 homes planned, per Boutique Hotelier. ICON's project page: finished N/A. El Cosmico's site, revised 22 September 2026: the original El Cosmico is closed, and the course it charted "isn't where we're headed after all."
ICC-ES ESR-4652, reissued June 2026, covers walls placed with ICON's Vulcan printer.
BIG (Wolf Ranch, El Cosmico, Performance Stage, Mars Dune Alpha), Lake|Flato (House Zero) and El Cosmico have built or designed with ICON. Collective Retreats manages El Cosmico.

code.line: The United States has an acceptance criterion and reports for printed walls. Canada, Mexico, Brazil and Chile have none specific to printing.

items.a: ICC-ES AC509 sets how printed concrete walls are evaluated: material, durability, structure and fire resistance. First approved December 2021.
ESR-4652, reissued June 2026, for the 2024, 2021 and 2018 IBC and IRC. It covers walls placed with ICON's Vulcan printer.

items.q: United States: the printer and process
items.a: UL 3401, Outline of Investigation for 3D Printed Building Construction, evaluates the printer, the process and the materials.
An optional appendix for printed construction: Appendix AW in the 2021 IRC, Appendix BM in the 2024 IRC. A jurisdiction must adopt it.
No printed wall system in the Canadian Construction Materials Centre's published evaluations, 28 September 2026. Projects have gone through local permits.
Budget 2024: $50 million through regional development agencies for projects including 3D printing, and a $50 million Homebuilding Technology and Innovation Fund.
Printed homes are certified under the same structural rules as conventional construction, with added testing.
No ABNT standard for printed construction, per Sika Brasil, 2024. New building systems in Minha Casa Minha Vida need a SINAT evaluation and a DATec.

trends.text: Mexico, Brazil and the Dominican Republic hold 61% of Latin America's hotel projects and 63% of its rooms, Q2 2026.
Upper upscale reached a record 133 projects and 22,869 rooms in Latin America's pipeline, Q2 2026.
97% of the rooms Mexico opened in the first half of 2025 were in Cancun and the Riviera Maya.
Quintana Roo has 135,754 hotel rooms, nearly 15% of Mexico's 909,719, 2025.
Hyatt Ziva Punta Cana: 650 rooms, opening 2029. The Dominican Republic received 11.6 million tourists in 2025.
Georgetown, Guyana had 16 hotel projects and 2,142 rooms in its pipeline at the end of 2025, level with Lima.
Branded residence schemes in the Caribbean and Latin America are forecast to grow 194% by 2032.
Glamping was 29% of North American camping experiences in 2025, and 31% of new campers chose it.
Canadian return trips from the US fell 25.4% in 2025. Overseas arrivals to Canada rose 7.5%.
South America's international arrivals grew 7% in 2025, the most of any subregion of the Americas.
Air arrivals at Guanacaste's airport rose 14.94% from January to April 2026.
Puerto Rico has $3.57 billion in disclosed investment attached to active hotel and branded residential projects.
Mexico's international tourism revenue is projected at US$36,800 million for 2026, up 5%.

brands.name: Postcard Cabins (Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy)
brands.detail: Marriott bought the Postcard Cabins brand (formerly Getaway) in December 2024: 29 outposts, 1,200+ cabins. The outposts run under long-term agreements with Marriott. Terms not disclosed.

brands.name: Trailborn (Outdoor Collection)
brands.detail: Long-term agreement announced December 2024 to add Trailborn's hotels to Marriott's system, alongside the Postcard Cabins purchase. Terms not disclosed.

brands.name: Design Hotels
brands.detail: Marriott's holding held more than 90% of Design Hotels AG in October 2020 and moved to squeeze out the remaining shareholders. Member hotels stay independent and book through Marriott Bonvoy.

sites.name: Terrestre, a Member of Design Hotels

brands.name: AutoCamp
brands.detail: Exclusive distribution partnership: AutoCamp stays are bookable on Hilton channels and earn Hilton Honors points. No equity stake was reported in the sources read.

brands.name: Small Luxury Hotels of the World (SLH)
brands.detail: Booking and distribution partnership, not an equity deal: participating SLH hotels (560 in 90 countries at signing) are bookable on Hilton channels.

sites.name: Los Altos Resort, an SLH Hotel
Alta Las Palomas, an SLH Hotel
Hotel Three Sixty, an SLH Hotel
The Retreat Costa Rica - Wellness Resort and Spa, an SLH Hotel

brands.name: Under Canvas
brands.detail: Exclusive partnership: Under Canvas camps join World of Hyatt for booking and loyalty. Under Canvas is backed by KSL Capital Partners (see KSL).

brands.name: Alila
brands.detail: Came with Hyatt's purchase of Two Roads Hospitality, closed November 30, 2018 at a revised $405 million base price. In June 2021 a Hyatt affiliate also bought the Alila Ventana Big Sur real estate for about $148 million.

sites.name: Ventana Big Sur, an Alila Resort

brands.name: Miraval
brands.detail: Hyatt bought Miraval Group from a KSL Capital Partners affiliate in January 2017, with plans to redevelop resorts in Austin, Texas and Lenox, Massachusetts.

brands.name: Ennismore
brands.detail: Accor holds 66.67% of Ennismore after an all-share merger closed in 2021; Sharan Pasricha holds 33.33%. Ennismore runs Delano, Hyde, SLS, Mondrian, The Hoxton, Mama Shelter, 21c and other lifestyle brands.

sites.name: Delano East Cape
sites.place: East Cape, Los Cabos, Baja California Sur

brands.name: Faena
brands.detail: Global strategic partnership between Accor and Faena Group (Alan Faena and Len Blavatnik) to develop Faena Districts; the venture also manages Faena Buenos Aires and Faena District Miami Beach. No equity stake figure found.

brands.name: 21c Museum Hotels
brands.detail: AccorHotels agreed to buy 85% of 21c Museum Hotels for $51 million including earn-out in July 2018; no real estate was included. 21c now sits in the Ennismore portfolio.

brands.name: Montage Hotels & Resorts
brands.detail: Montage manages; owners and developers build. Montage Valle de Guadalupe (announced December 2025) is developed with Thor Urbana and Life Properties International, which also partnered on Montage Los Cabos.

sites.name: Montage Valle de Guadalupe
sites.place: Bruma Wine Estate, Valle de Guadalupe, Baja California

brands.name: Pendry Hotels & Resorts
brands.detail: Montage International's second brand. Pendry Punta Mita is in development alongside Montage Punta Mita.

brands.name: Cayuga Collection
brands.detail: Operator of sustainable small hotels in Central America for over two decades; lists seven hotels in four countries. Several hotels have separate owners.

brands.name: Nayara
brands.detail: Costa Rican resort group with three Arenal resorts. In October 2020 it took on Tánica's two Chilean hotels as its first joint ventures with Tánica; it also runs Nayara Bocas del Toro in Panama.

brands.name: Aman
brands.detail: Vladislav Doronin has owned Aman since August 2015 and settled the ownership court dispute in March 2016. Aman runs six Americas and Caribbean properties, including a 10-tent glamping camp in Utah.

brands.name: Vik Retreats
brands.detail: Hotel and winery group of Alex and Carrie Vik, who design their own properties: three in José Ignacio, Uruguay, two at the VIK vineyard in Chile's Millahue Valley, plus Galleria Vik in Milan.

brands.name: Six Senses
brands.detail: IHG completed the purchase of Six Senses Hotels Resorts Spas on February 12, 2019 for $300 million in cash. Six Senses manages its resorts under agreements with local owners.

brands.name: Curamoria Collection
brands.detail: Boutique brand launched by Grupo Posadas in 2020. Náay Tulum was its first hotel.

brands.name: Hoteles Xcaret
brands.detail: Grupo Xcaret, the Riviera Maya park operator, owns and runs its own hotels: 1,863 suites in three hotels in September 2022. La Casa de la Playa cost US$80 million.

brands.name: Awasi
brands.detail: Villa-based lodge group; Awasi Atacama opened 2007. In 2025 it added two operating hotels it renamed: Ponta dos Ganchos in Brazil and Cavas Wine Lodge in Argentina, for five lodges.

brands.name: Grupo Habita hotels
brands.detail: Design hotel group founded by Carlos Couturier with Jaime, Moisés and Rafael Micha; 17 hotels in Mexico and the US as of 2026. Its hotels are Design Hotels members, booked through Marriott Bonvoy (see Marriott).

brands.name: Inkaterra
brands.detail: Peruvian eco-hotel group founded by José Koechlin in 1975. IDB Invest approved a US$12 million senior secured loan in November 2024 (signed December 2024) to build Cabo Blanco and Machu Picchu and add Amazon rooms.

brands.name: Anantara
brands.detail: Minor's first Anantara in the Americas, announced May 2026: a resort with 78 branded residences on North Caicos, opening 2029. Owners include Octans and local developer Rob Ayer.

sites.name: Anantara Turks and Caicos Resort & Residences

brands.name: Under Canvas
brands.detail: A KSL affiliate made a 'substantial investment' in Under Canvas in December 2018, when it had eight camps; terms not disclosed. By June 2026 it ran 17 locations across three brands. KSL earlier owned Miraval, sold to Hyatt in 2017.

brands.name: Beckons (Baillie Lodges and Tierra Hotels)
brands.detail: KSL-backed Baillie Lodges bought a majority of Chile's Tierra Hotels in August 2022. In March 2026 the two were merged under a new brand, Beckons: nine lodges in Australia, New Zealand, Chile and Canada.

sites.name: Tierra Patagonia
sites.place: Lake Sarmiento, Torres del Paine, Magallanes

brands.name: Auberge Resorts Collection
brands.detail: Dan Friedkin is chairman of Auberge Collection, per Auberge's March 2026 release on The Stockman. Its site lists 6 resorts in Mexico, the Caribbean and Central America.

brands.name: AutoCamp
brands.detail: Whitman Peterson led a $115 million dedicated capital commitment in early 2019 to buy and redevelop sites for AutoCamp, enough to develop over $500 million in projects. AutoCamp founded 2013; bookable on Hilton since 2024.

brands.name: Explora
brands.detail: Explora is a company of Grupo Córpora, owned by the Ibáñez family (Diario Financiero, May 2018). It runs all-inclusive lodges in Chile, Argentina, Peru and Bolivia; architect José Cruz Ovalle designs them in wood.

sites.name: Explora Torres del Paine Conservation Reserve

brands.name: Rosewood Hotels & Resorts
brands.detail: RLH (BMV: RLH A) owns the hotel real estate; Rosewood Hotel Group, privately owned by Chow Tai Fook Enterprises, manages. RLH built Rosewood Mandarina, which opened in 2025.

sites.name: Rosewood Mayakoba
sites.place: Mayakoba, Playa del Carmen, Quintana Roo

brands.name: One&Only
brands.detail: RLH owns One&Only Mandarina and sells One&Only-branded homes at Mandarina.

brands.detail: JHSF, the listed Brazilian developer, owns the Fasano hotel brand: eight hotels in Brazil plus Punta del Este and New York in August 2024. In April 2026 it agreed to buy the Enjoy Punta del Este complex to add a Fasano hotel, casino and homes.
